title: FilePicker validation is bypassed on forward navigation and cleared by Group refresh
fix(select): update key bindings when Filtering(true) is set before WithKeyMap
body:
## Summary

Fixes #854.

`Select.Filtering(true)` only set the `filtering` flag; it never updated the enabled
state of the filter-related key bindings. A `Select` configured with
`Filtering(true)` **before** being attached to a form kept the key map's default
non-filtering bindings after `Group.WithKeyMap` assigned the default
`SelectKeyMap` (`Filter`/`/` enabled, `SetFilter`/Esc and `ClearFilter`/Esc
disabled). Esc therefore did not leave the initial filter mode, and the keys
pressed afterwards were typed into the filter input, leaving the option list
empty. The help line also kept advertising `/ filter` while filter mode was
already active.

## Root cause

In `field_select.go`:

- `Filtering(true)` wrote `s.filtering = true` and focused the filter input, but
  the key bindings determine which keys `Update` reacts to:
  - `/` matches `s.keymap.Filter` (`setFiltering(true)`).
  - Esc matches `s.keymap.SetFilter` (`setFiltering(false)`).
- The default `SelectKeyMap` (assigned later via `NewDefaultKeyMap()` and
  `WithKeyMap`) creates `SetFilter` disabled and `Filter` enabled.
- `WithKeyMap` replaced `s.keymap` wholesale and only adjusted the inline /
  positional bindings, discarding the binding state implied by
  `s.filtering == true`.

In an initial-filter-mode field, pressing Esc never matched a binding, so
`setFiltering(false)` was never called. The following `j` key was then handled by
the filter `textinput`; no option matched the filter text, `filteredOptions`
became empty, and `Hovered()` returned `("", false)`.

## Fix

- `Filtering(bool)` now routes through the existing `setFiltering(bool)` helper
  instead of assigning the flag directly, so bindings reflect the requested
  state immediately.
- `WithKeyMap` reconciles the filter bindings at the end of the assignment with
  `s.setFiltering(s.filtering)`, so any key map assigned after the builder call
  (which is exactly what `NewForm` does during construction) keeps the field in
  the correct mode.
- A select that does not use initial filter mode keeps its previous binding
  state, because `setFiltering(false)` reproduces the default states.

```go
func (s *Select[T]) Filtering(filtering bool) *Select[T] {
	s.setFiltering(filtering)
	s.filter.Focus()
	return s
}

func (s *Select[T]) WithKeyMap(k *KeyMap) Field {
	s.keymap = k.Select
	// ...existing inline/position bits...
	s.setFiltering(s.filtering)
	return s
}
```

After this change, an initial-filter-mode select shows
`esc set filter` in its help line (instead of `/ filter`); Esc leaves filter mode,
the help line returns to the normal set including `/ filter`, and navigation keys
move between options again.

## Tests

New regression tests in `field_select_test.go`:

- `TestSelectInitialFilteringKeyMap` — covers all construction orders (filter
  option set before the key map, after the key map, and implicitly via
  `NewForm(NewGroup(field))`): starting binding states, Esc leaving filter mode,
  binding state afterwards, and `j` navigating to `two`.
- `TestSelectEscWithoutFilterMode` — guards the pre-existing behavior for a
  select that does not start in filter mode.
- `TestSelectInitialFilteringHelp` — verifies the rendered help line contains
  `esc set filter` while in initial filter mode and `/ filter` after Esc.

Verification (locally):

- `go test -count=1 ./...` — pass on Go 1.25.8 (the version pinned in
  `go.mod`) and Go 1.25.14.
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...` — pass.
- `go vet ./...` — clean.
- `gofumpt -l .` / `goimports -l .` — clean.
- `golangci-lint run --config=.golangci.yml --timeout=10m ./...`
  (golangci-lint v2.15.0) — `0 issues`.
- `cd examples && go build ./...` — pass.

Before the source change, the new tests fail on `main` in all three key-map
construction orders (`SetFilter` unexpectedly disabled, `Filter` unexpectedly
enabled, Esc not leaving filter mode, hovered option empty); after the change
they pass, and the complete existing suite remains green.

## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI programming-agent help on the contributor's
account: the agent reproduced the issue, diagnosed the binding-initialization
problem, implemented and validated the fix and tests above. I reviewed every
changed line and take responsibility for the contribution.

title: feat(select,multiselect): add MaxHeight and fix default viewport height (#856)
body:
### Summary

This PR addresses #856 by adding `MaxHeight(height int)` to both `Select` and `MultiSelect`.

### Problem

Currently, `Height(height int)` enforces a fixed height in terminal lines:
- For short lists, it pads the component with blank lines up to the specified height.
- On narrow terminals where option labels wrap across multiple lines, options exceed the fixed line count and get cut off or truncated.
- Callers cannot know terminal width beforehand to calculate the wrapped option line count at field construction time.

Additionally, in `MultiSelect.updateViewportSize()`, `yoffset` (title/description height) was being subtracted from the options height even when `height <= 0`, which caused options at the bottom of the list to be cut off under default settings.

### Solution

1. Added `.MaxHeight(height int)` to `Select` and `MultiSelect`:
   - Binds the maximum height of the field without forcing empty padding for shorter lists.
   - Dynamically sizes the viewport up to `MaxHeight`, allowing multiline wrapped options to display without being cut off on narrow terminals.
   - When content exceeds `MaxHeight`, the viewport scrolls as expected.
2. Fixed `MultiSelect.updateViewportSize()` so `yoffset` is only subtracted when `height > 0`.
3. Added unit tests in `huh_test.go` covering wrapped options, short lists, and bounds checks for both components.

Fixes #856

title: fix: sync select filter bindings when keymap is applied
body:
Fixes #854.

## Problem

`Select.Filtering(true)` sets the filtering state directly, but the filter keybindings are only enabled in `setFiltering`, which runs when the user presses `/`. Since a form applies `WithKeyMap` to its fields after they are built, the replacement keymap always carries the default binding states. A field built with `Filtering(true)` therefore keeps the wrong bindings: Esc does nothing until the user presses `/` or Enter, and the help line shows `/ filter` for a filter that is already open.

## Fix

Re-sync the binding states with the current filtering state at the end of `WithKeyMap` by calling `s.setFiltering(s.filtering)`. A field that starts in filter mode now behaves as if `/` had been pressed: Esc leaves filter mode, `/` is disabled while filtering, and the help line is correct. Fields not in filter mode are unaffected because `setFiltering(false)` reproduces the default binding states.

## Tests

Added `TestSelectFilteringTrueEscLeavesFilter`, which builds a select with `Filtering(true)`, applies the default keymap, sends Esc and then `j`, and asserts the cursor moves to the next option instead of typing into the filter. The test fails without the fix (`after Esc and j, hovered "", want two`) and passes with it. The full `charm.land/huh/v2` package test suite passes.
